name: Flash flooding from extreme rain – Halifax region

geo.extent: Halifax Regional Municipality and central Nova Scotia

description: In July 2023, 100 mm in one hour and 173 mm in six hours fell in Bedford (Halifax), a national rainfall record per ECCC; four people died. Halifax's summer rainfall that year was 619 mm, about twice normal.

exposed_areas: Bedford, Sackville and other Halifax-area communities along small rivers
documented_events: July 2023: 100 mm/1 h and 173 mm/6 h in Bedford; 4 deaths (ECCC 2023)
practical_implications: Small-river and urban flooding; basement flooding risk

sources.title: Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: Single event. Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
